red_flag_options.label: Blood or dark tar-like stool visible
Vomiting or retching alongside diarrhea
Pet is unusually limp, unresponsive, or extremely weak
Suspected ingestion of toxic plants, chemicals, or foreign items
Pet is a very young puppy/kitten under 12 weeks
Gums are pale, white, or blue instead of healthy pink

home_care_steps: Keep fresh, clean water accessible at all times to prevent dehydration.
Withhold food for 12-24 hours for adult dogs ONLY (never fast puppies, kittens, or seniors).
Once feeding resumes, offer small bland meals (plain boiled chicken breast and plain white rice) for 2 to 3 days.
Ensure quiet rest in a warm, comfortable room.
Track frequency, color, and consistency of bowel movements for your vet.
escalation_message: If diarrhea persists past 24 hours, contains blood, or your pet exhibits lethargy, seek veterinary care promptly.

red_flag_options.label: Repeated non-stop retching without anything coming up (bloat risk)
Vomiting bright red blood or coffee-ground material
Suspected swallowing of toys, string, socks, or human medicine
Abdomen looks swollen, hard, or hurts when touched
Pet cannot stand or is severely lethargic

home_care_steps: Withhold food for 6-12 hours for adult pets; allow tiny licks of water or ice chips.
Never withhold water for young puppies, kittens, or seniors for more than 2-3 hours without vet advice.
Reintroduce small portions of bland food (plain chicken & rice or prescribed recovery food) gradually.
Do not give any over-the-counter human medicines.
escalation_message: Single episodes of vomiting can happen, but repeated vomiting within hours requires immediate vet evaluation.

red_flag_options.label: Unresponsive or barely opens eyes when called or touched
Collapsed or unable to support weight on legs
Rapid, heavy, or open-mouth panting/gasping breathing
Gums are pale gray, blue, or deep purple

home_care_steps: Provide a peaceful, dark, stress-free sleeping area with fresh water nearby.
Gently check capillary refill time (press gum for 2 sec; pink color should return within 2 seconds).
Encourage light hydration with water or ice cubes.
Record temperature if you have a digital pet thermometer.
escalation_message: Lethargy lasting more than 24 hours is a primary sign of underlying illness and warrants a professional checkup.

red_flag_options.label: Facial swelling, swollen muzzle, or hives after insect sting
Hot spots with active bleeding, open sores, or deep skin tears
Pus, yellow discharge, or foul smell from ears or skin folds

home_care_steps: Inspect coat for visible fleas, ticks, or burrs.
Use an Elizabethan collar (cone) to prevent self-mutilation or biting at hot spots.
Wipe paws and coat with a damp warm towel after outdoor walks to clear environmental pollen.
Ensure flea and tick preventative is up to date.
escalation_message: If skin redness worsens or turns into moist hot spots, schedule a vet appointment for allergy or infection evaluation.

red_flag_options.label: Open-mouth breathing, flaring nostrils, or abdominal effort to breathe
Gums or tongue are blue/purple (lack of oxygen)
Coughing up foam, blood, or pinkish fluid
High-pitched choking noise or inability to get air

home_care_steps: Keep pet indoors in a clean, smoke-free, dust-free environment.
Allow pet to sit in a humid bathroom while running a warm shower (steam therapy for 10-15 min).
Keep nose and eyes gently clean using a soft moist cotton pad.
Isolate from other household pets if infectious kennel cough / upper respiratory infection is suspected.
escalation_message: Persistent coughing can indicate kennel cough, feline asthma, or heart conditions. See a vet if coughing persists.

red_flag_options.label: Completely non-weight bearing or holding leg up high
Limb appears bent, misaligned, or fractured
Vocalizing, crying, or snapping when leg is touched
Hind leg is cold to touch or dragged (Feline Aortic Thromboembolism risk in cats)

home_care_steps: Restrict activity immediately: keep pet strictly on leash or in a comfortable small room/crate.
Inspect paw pads carefully for thorns, cut pads, or torn nails.
Do NOT attempt to splint, bandage tightly, or give human pain medications (ibuprofen/paracetamol are extremely toxic).
Apply cold compress to minor joint swelling for 10-15 minutes if pet tolerates it.
escalation_message: Limping that does not improve after 24 hours of rest requires orthopedic examination and X-rays by a veterinarian.

red_flag_options.label: Eye surface looks hazy, cloudy blue, or ulcerated
Eye is squinted shut or pet rubs eye constantly against carpet
Eye socket appears swollen, protruding, or enlarged
Visible scratch, cut, or foreign debris in eye

home_care_steps: Place an Elizabethan collar (cone) on pet immediately to prevent pawing and corneal scratch worsening.
Gently wipe outer tear drainage from around the eye using plain sterile saline on a clean gauze.
Do not use leftover human or old pet eye drops.
escalation_message: Eye injuries escalate rapidly into corneal ulcers or vision loss. Prompt vet evaluation is critical for squinting or cloudy eyes.
